title: Customer Voices - Rapid Scan (mixed-methods): Feedback & Feature Signals, Apr 2024
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, mixed-methods rapid scan of customer feedback collected between 2024-02 and 2024-04 to surface near-term product signals for the roadmap. The goal is to translate recurring asks into clear, prioritized feature concepts and suggested owners for quick validation cycles.

Methods and data sources
- Support tickets: random sample of 180 tickets tagged "inference" and "performance" (Feb-Apr 2024).
- Sales + AE calls: notes from 12 enterprise discovery meetings (recordings + transcripts).
- CS field visits: 3 customer onsite debriefs (notes).
- In-product telemetry: API error spikes, latency histograms, and model fallback rates (prod telemetry, anonymized).
- NPS verbatims: aggregated open responses (Q1 2024).
- Engineering triage: 6 internal bug tickets linked to customer reports.

Executive summary (top-line takeaways)
- Two primary customer pain clusters: (A) Predictable latency under mixed workloads, especially for embedded/concurrent real-time use cases; (B) Confusing model variant choices + unclear cost/quality tradeoffs.
- High-frequency, high-value asks: improved latency SLO visibility per route, and an automated suggestion for batching/quantization profiles per workload.
- Confidence: medium-high (consistent across telemetry + direct customer statements). Several asks are already in product backlog but lack clear prioritization and owning team.

Top themes and signal strength
1) Latency predictability for mixed workloads (strong signal)
   - Evidence: 42 support tickets mention "latency spikes when concurrent jobs run", telemetry shows 95th %-ile jumps during burst windows.
   - Impact: customers building chat or agent experiences report user-visible stalls.
   - Representative quote: "Works great in demo, but in production when other teams hit the cluster our latency doubles — users notice immediately."

2) Better guidance for model variants / quantization (medium-strong)
   - Evidence: sales notes and NPS verbatims repeatedly say "which model should I pick?" and "I don’t know if quantized route will break our prompts."
   - Impact: customers delay rollouts or overpay for larger instances.

3) Observability at route + token granularity (medium)
   - Evidence: requests for per-route token cost breakdowns tied to prompts; console tickets asking for example traces from token -> request mapping.
   - Impact: teams can’t correlate cost regressions with recent prompt changes or model rollouts.

4) Graceful fallback behavior clarity (emerging)
   - Evidence: customers hit fallbacks to smaller models under capacity constraints and are surprised by output differences.
   - Impact: production error handling is brittle; few customers have automated A/B fallback guards.

Feature request compendium (condensed entries)
- Feature: Route-level latency SLO dashboard (90/95/99 pctl)  Priority: P0-P1 depending on customer (enterprises = P0); Signal: strong  Rough effort: medium (console + backend aggregation)  Suggested owner: product-console + observability eng  Acceptance: per-route time-series, alerting, ability to pin SLO in rollouts.

- Feature: Automated workload profiler + batching/quantization recommendation engine  Priority: P0 for heavy-cost customers, P1 for others  Signal: strong (telemetry + repeated requests)  Rough effort: large (ML + infra + UI)  Suggested owner: eng-applied-ml + optimize product team  Acceptance: profiler outputs recommended config and estimated cost savings with one-click apply to staging.

- Feature: Model-variant explainer and guardrails in Console  Priority: P1  Signal: medium  Rough effort: small-medium (docs + UI + simple evals)  Suggested owner: developer-experience + product-hosted-api  Acceptance: clear selector with quality vs cost tradeoff, sample outputs for user prompt, and quick rollback.

- Feature: Token-level cost trace linking prompts -> cost + latency  Priority: P1  Signal: medium  Rough effort: medium  Suggested owner: observability + console  Acceptance: downloadable CSVs, per-request traces up to 30 days.

Quick wins (can be delivered in 4-6 weeks)
- Publish a short "model variant decision guide" in Console: pick a default set of recommendations for common workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings). Owner: developer-experience.
- Add a simple latency heatmap to existing route pages (shows p50/p95 by hour). Owner: console team.
- Create a standard support playbook for fallback incidents (CS + SRE): steps to detect, notify, and rollback. Owner: customer-success + SRE.

Risks and unknowns
- Telemetry gaps: we do not consistently tag token streams by tenant route in all regions — some metrics are noisy. Need engineering input to estimate instrumentation cost.
- Customer mental model: several customers believe "quantized=bad quality"; the true quality delta depends on prompt and model. We need short evals to show concrete examples.
- Capacity constraints: some proposed automation (auto-apply batching) could increase tail latency for other tenants if not throttled; will require coordination with serving-runtime.

Suggested immediate actions (next 30 days)
1) Kick a 3-week discovery sprint for the workload profiler idea: define MVP, run with 2 pilot customers (AE-sourced). Owner: applied-ml + solutions-engineering.
2) Ship the model variant decision guide and add it to onboarding flow. Owner: developer-experience.
3) Instrument per-route p95 in a single region and add the basic heatmap widget to console. Owner: observability + console.
4) CS: run follow-up interviews (5 customers) to validate that the profiler output maps to perceived improvements. Owner: customer-success.

Appendix: notable verbatims (anonymized)
- "We tried the smaller model after quantization and it was fine for embeddings but hallucinated more on QA prompts. Need clarity."
- "Our ops team wants an SLA we can actually map to a route, not the whole account."
- "If you could suggest the batching window and quantization for our prompt, we’d try it immediately."

Who to loop in now
- Product: console + optimize
- Engineering: applied-ml, serving-runtime, observability
- GTM: solutions engineering for pilot recruitment

Open questions for the next review
- What telemetry tags are cheapest to add to get consistent per-route token tracing?
- Which two customers are highest-signal for a profiler pilot (cost + willingness to try experimental optimizations)?

Notes to self
- Cross-check JIRA tickets listed in linked_artifacts with telemetry windows before sprint kickoff.
- Prepare 2 short demo prompts for each pilot to show cost/quality tradeoffs at a glance.

End of rapid scan.
